Business Analyst isn’t just another corporate job—it’s one of the fastest‑growing paths for people who mix business sense with data skills. Entry‑level analysts typically start around ₹6–10 LPA, especially if they know Excel, basic SQL, and dashboards (Power BI/Tableau). With 3–5 years of experience plus strong SQL, data visualization, and stakeholder management, that range usually grows to roughly ₹12–20 LPA across IT, consulting, and finance.

By the mid‑level (5–8 years), analysts working in consulting, fintech, and product companies often move into Senior/Lead roles earning about ₹20–35 LPA, handling ownership of metrics, roadmaps, and decision support. Top‑end Lead Business Analysts, Product Consultants, or Managers can cross ₹40 LPA and beyond, especially in large enterprises or high‑growth tech firms. description:
LTX Studio by Lightricks is changing the way AI-powered video production works. Unlike many AI video generators that act like black boxes, LTX Studio gives creators real control over their content. From script-to-scene generation to camera angle adjustments and lighting control, this platform is built for filmmakers, marketers, and content creators who want precision in AI storytelling. It also supports asset management and integrates LTX-2 technology with NVIDIA acceleration for faster rendering and improved privacy.
While LTX Studio is excellent for rapid prototyping and storyboarding, it does come with limitations. Video length is currently capped at around 20 seconds, and some users report occasional motion inconsistencies or minor glitches. However, for creators looking to experiment, visualize ideas quickly, and maintain character consistency across scenes, it remains a powerful tool.

Did you know India just made a massive statement in the AI world? Sarvam AI, a Bengaluru-based startup, has shocked the tech community by beating global giants like ChatGPT and Google Gemini with just $41 million in funding! At the AI Summit in Delhi, Sarvam outperformed these tech titans despite having only 3 billion parameters compared to Google’s 2 trillion. But what sets Sarvam apart? They focused on India’s real needs – regional language processing, authentic Indian accents, and complex document reading.

Sarvam’s real-world impact is undeniable. With the launch of Shoka V1, India’s first audio language model, and Bulbul V2, a text-to-speech engine that sounds human, they’re solving problems like reading forms and decoding handwritten notes. They even made strides globally with Bharat GPT Mini, an AI model for low-power devices, making waves at Vivatech Paris.
